description:
A 10-second vertical anime sequence: the climax of a dark-fantasy anime in which the hero steals the king's crown. It will be cut apart and intercut with other footage in the edit, so it MUST be MULTI-SHOT: six distinct setups, each numbered beat its own shot, joined by clean hard cuts. Do not make it one continuous take.

STYLE — high-end seasonal TV action anime, the look of a top-studio fantasy series at its climax: crisp confident linework, rich cel shading with two shadow tones, strong coloured rim light, painterly detailed backgrounds, dramatic lighting, shallow depth of field, a touch of film grain. Colour: deep night blues and cold moonlight from the windows against warm gold candlelight; the crown and the king's armour catch hot gold highlights; one deep crimson accent in the hero's coat lining. Not 3D, not CG, not Western cartoon, not chibi, not glossy plastic.

SETTING — a vast gothic throne room at night in a storm. Rain streams down enormous stained-glass windows of abstract coloured glass (no figures, no symbols). Tall stone pillars, iron candelabras, a long crimson carpet running up to a raised dais with a massive dark-and-gold throne. Lightning flickers behind the glass.

CHARACTERS — identical in every beat they appear in:
- THE HERO: a young man of about 19, messy dark-brown hair falling over his forehead, warm brown eyes, expressive eyebrows, a small thin scar on his left cheekbone. Long black coat with crimson lining and thin gold trim, black trousers, dark boots, a sword in a black scabbard at his left hip, sheathed until the final beat. Handsome in an approachable way, not a pretty-boy.
- KING AURELIUS: a beautiful, arrogant young king of about 25, long straight pale-blond hair past his shoulders, cool blue eyes, fine features. White-and-gold ceremonial plate armour with gold filigree and a white fur-trimmed cloak. Calm, still, contemptuous. He never shouts.
- THE CROWN: one ornate gold crown with tall pointed spires and deep red gems. THERE IS ONLY EVER ONE CROWN. It starts on the king's head; once the hero takes it, the king is bareheaded for the rest of the piece and the crown stays on the hero's head. Never show a second crown.
- THE GUARDS: royal guards in silver plate armour with dark-blue tabards and closed visored helmets, so no faces are ever visible. Never more than four guards clearly in frame; any others are soft, out-of-focus silhouettes deep in the background. Each holds exactly one longsword.

TEXT RULE — no words, letters, numbers, symbols, interface, subtitles or logos anywhere in any frame.

The story, in order:

1. (about 1.2 s) Extreme close-up of the gold crown sitting on King Aurelius's pale-blond head. The hero's hand darts in from the lower left, snatches the crown straight off and pulls it out of frame; a few blond strands lift in its wake. Static camera. One hand, one crown.

2. (about 1.5 s) Medium shot on the dais. The hero, standing in front of the throne, calmly lowers the crown onto his own messy dark-brown hair with both hands. Behind him, seated on the throne, the now bareheaded king's eyes go wide. Slow push in.

3. (about 1.4 s) Wide low-angle shot from the carpet: the hero stands at the centre wearing the crown, the bareheaded king on the throne behind him. Four guards around him snap their longswords out at the same instant, blades flashing in the candlelight. Static camera.

4. (about 2.2 s) Close-up of King Aurelius on his throne, bareheaded, candlelight on his face. His expression moves from surprise, to stillness, to a slow, faint, impressed smile, and then he speaks one short quiet sentence, lips moving only briefly. Very slow push in.

5. (about 1.6 s) Medium close-up of the hero, crown on his head, surrounded: guards' sword tips point at him from both edges of the frame. His eyes go wide and he glances left, then right — a comic 'oh no' look. Static camera.

6. (about 2.1 s) Close on the hero's face as the guards charge at him, soft and blurred in the background. He draws his sword up into a guard and breaks into a wide, reckless grin, crown still on his head. Fast push in toward his face; the hero himself barely moves.

AUDIO: storm rain against the glass throughout; a bright metallic clink as the crown is snatched; one ringing SHING as the swords are drawn together; heavy armoured footsteps as the guards charge; a low, tense orchestral anime score underneath the whole piece. No spoken words, no voices, no narration — the king's line is added in post, so his lips move silently.
